images.title: Taking away chikki pieces
images.purpose: Show that taking away fractions with the same unit means taking away equal pieces: the count of pieces changes and the unit 1/7 stays.
images.composition: One long chikki bar across the upper middle with wide space around it, a small group of lifted pieces to its lower right, and one equation centred below.
images.exact_structure: One flat rectangular chikki bar cut by straight lines into exactly 7 equal pieces. The 2 leftmost pieces are filled teal #0072B2 and stay in the bar. The next 4 pieces are filled amber #E69F00 and are drawn lifted out, sitting together in a row below and to the right of the bar with a clear gap. The 7th piece is an empty outline in the bar. The 4 amber pieces are exactly the same size as the teal pieces. Below, centred: one equation line. Exactly 1 bar, 7 equal pieces, 2 teal, 4 amber, 1 empty.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
chikki pieces that are not all exactly equal in size
images.takeaway: Take away the pieces; the unit stays the same.
images.description: A chikki bar cut into 7 equal pieces: 6 pieces were Tanvi's, 4 amber pieces are lifted away to Joseph and 2 teal pieces stay, so 6/7 − 4/7 = 2/7.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the teal pieces left in the bar and say what one piece is called.

image_decisions.why: Taking equal pieces away from a cut bar is a picture idea; one clean image shows the unit staying the same.
